tools.name: sprint_summary
tools.description: One sprint as the Sprint Summary view counts it: delivered items and points, cycle time, carryover, and commitment (committed at the end of day one, completed of committed, reliability, scope added and removed). Answers with numbers, dates, states and work item ids only; never work item titles, descriptions, comments, tags or assigned people, and never calls Baytek. Uses the customer’s saved workflow mapping only; no mapping answers {"error":"workflow-not-mapped"}. {"error":"licence-inactive"} means the organisation’s trial has ended without a valid licence, or its licence has not been confirmed for 30 days: tell the person to open Agile Analytics in Azure DevOps and, if the answer stays the same, to ask an admin to look at Configuration → License. {"error":"no-seat"} means the plan gives Agile Analytics to assigned people only and this person has no seat: tell them to open Agile Analytics in Azure DevOps once and ask again and, if the answer stays the same, to ask an extension admin for a seat (Configuration → Access Control). {"error":"throttled"} or {"error":"timed-out"}: wait a minute and ask again.

sprintId.description: Iteration GUID. Default: the last finished sprint (a running sprint is never summarised by default).

tools.name: forecast
tools.description: Monte Carlo forecast from the throughput of the finished sprints among the last 12: how many items in a window, or when a backlog finishes. sampleSprints is how many sprints it drew from: say that number with the forecast. The hub’s Monte Carlo view and Dashboard start from the 6 newest finished sprints, so their figures can differ from this one. backlog.description: when: number of items to finish.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Checks what the connector needs before it can answer, in the order every tool checks it, and reports each check as a fixed word: sign-in, extension settings, admin switch, licence, seat, the workflow mapping (only when a project and team are given) and the plan (open = the Premium extras are included). A check after one that failed is not-checked. Call it when a tool answers an error, or to set up. Answers fixed words only and never calls Baytek.
